title: Work-efficient parallel approximate flow
formal:
Does undirected vertex-capacitated maximum flow admit a uniform randomized parallel \((1+\varepsilon)\)-approximation with nearly-linear total work and polylogarithmic depth?

Given an undirected graph with \(n\) vertices and \(m\) edges, distinct terminals \(s,t\), and nonnegative vertex capacities, the algorithm must output a feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow of value at least \(\mathrm{OPT}/(1+\varepsilon)\), where \(\mathrm{OPT}\) is the maximum feasible flow value. It must use \((n+m)\operatorname{polylog}n\) work (total processor operations) and \(\operatorname{polylog}n\) depth (parallel steps), with success probability at least \(2/3\).

The polynomially bounded capacities, inverse-polylogarithmic accuracy regime, uniformity and word-PRAM model are quantified below.
